title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia leaving her role a week after starting it: official
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's press secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving her role a mere week after he put her in the role, a White House official confirmed to CBC News.

image.caption: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia seen at Glacier Park International Airport on Wednesday in Kalispell, Mont. U.S. President Donald Trump has since said Zacharia may want to reconsider her role following intense media scrutiny. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: U.S. President Donald Trump's press secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving her role a mere week after he put her in the role, a White House official confirmed to CBC News.
U.S. President Trump said Zacharia was 'brutalized by the media' during her first week
More to come. Previous version below.
U.S. President Donald Trump signalled Friday that his embattled new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, may be on her way out — a mere week after he picked her for the post.
Speaking to reporters on the White House lawn as he left for a rally in Georgia, Trump said he’d spoken to Zacharia and that he felt she didn’t deserve what he called negative media coverage.
"I told her, 'I think you’re better off being happy,'" Trump said.
“We’re talking about — I want her to have a good life. I don’t want her to have a life like she’s led the last three days,” Trump said.

Trump added, "I said, 'Katie, do you need this? I don’t think you need this.'"
The president said he’d make a final determination later perhaps after his campaign travel, adding, "When I get back, we’re going to talk."

items: Katie Zacharia fails to impress in brief debut as White House press secretary

blocks.text: He also said, "I told Katie, in my opinion, she was treated very unfairly," Trump said, noting that Zacharia has been "brutalized by the media."
